tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative 'Use it when...' phrasing, focuses on user-facing triggers (access errors, model lifecycle questions, KB returning stale/empty answers) rather than implementation mechanics, explicitly pushes for broad coverage ('Use it even if they don't name invocation logging, SCPs, chunking, embeddings or vector stores'), and explicitly excludes adjacent scopes. It is dense but stays within a short paragraph and is clearly actionable for triggering.
tests.evidence: Use it when a Bedrock call fails with an access, validation or throttling error, no one can see what the model does, a model may be end-of-life... Use it even if they don't name invocation logging, SCPs, chunking, embeddings or vector stores.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays domain-specific throughout: it explains the two review areas, the account-ID masking rule, severity definitions, and routing logic, without ever explaining generic concepts like what an API or IAM role is. Some sections (Guardrails, When to Use) are long but each line conveys a specific, non-obvious constraint rather than generic background.
tests.evidence: "Never write the 12-digit account ID anywhere in text... Write `the account under review` (or its alias)."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables, error-code catalogs, or metric thresholds are embedded in the body; the detailed catalogs (LLM-INV-001..015, LLM-KB-001..012, metrics, API quirks) are all delegated to references/ files and only routing tables/pointers appear in the body.
tests.evidence: Severity table and routing table are short and generic; detailed catalogs live in "checks-model-invocation.md" and "checks-rag-knowledgebase.md", linked but not embedded.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked with a markdown link in the References section and/or the routing table.
tests.evidence: "[model-access-review.md](references/model-access-review.md)", "[api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md)", "[related-skills.md](references/related-skills.md)" etc. — all 9 reference files are linked.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link in the References section and routing table explains precisely when to load it (e.g., before raising a finding, while running a step, when interpreting a response).
tests.evidence: "[checks-model-invocation.md](references/checks-model-invocation.md): load before raising any LLM-INV finding (the LLM-INV-001..015 catalog)."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, safety-critical operations (account-ID masking, read-only guardrails, chunk-content suppression) are given exact, non-negotiable prescriptive language, while flexible decisions (which area to run, how to phrase an answer) are left to the agent's judgment with rationale given.
tests.evidence: "Read-only. Never call a mutating API... never call `StartIngestionJob`" vs. "When a question spans both areas, run both reviews and present one report..."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The routing table presents a clear decision path to a single area/file per question type rather than listing multiple equal tool options; no competing tool choices are presented as a menu.
tests.evidence: Routing table maps each question type to exactly one "Area" and "Read first" file, not multiple equal alternatives.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable approach (pick area, read review file, run checks, cite check-ids, bound scope) that applies across many different Bedrock/RAG questions rather than declaring one specific instance's answer.
tests.evidence: "Name the area, then read its review file **before the first API call**... Each file holds the router, the step-by-step procedure..."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: While there's no section literally titled 'Gotchas,' the Guardrails section and inline notes (e.g., distinguishing 'measured zero' from 'no data reported', INFERENCE_PROFILE-only models, access-denied vs throttling distinctions between areas) function as concrete, environment-specific pitfall corrections.
tests.evidence: "Distinguish 'measured zero' from 'no data reported' or 'no job to read'" and "when it is `INFERENCE_PROFILE` only, say that every bare-ID call to it fails, not that it is merely suboptimal."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces posture reports and provides dedicated templates in assets/ for both review areas, satisfying the need for structured output.
tests.evidence: "[bedrock-configuration-report-template.md](assets/bedrock-configuration-report-template.md) and [rag-health-report-template.md](assets/rag-health-report-template.md): load only when the user asks for a full written report"

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No inline report templates or format skeletons appear in the SKILL.md body; the actual templates are stored in assets/ and loaded conditionally.
tests.evidence: Templates are only linked, not embedded: "load only when the user asks for a full written report, one per area."

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both asset files are referenced in the body — once in the routing table and once in the References section.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset links specify precisely when to load them: only when the user requests a full written report.
tests.evidence: "load only when the user asks for a full written report, one per area."

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: Asset references use relative paths of the form assets/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The SKILL.md body itself does not present a single ordered, dependent step-by-step procedure that needs checklist tracking; it is primarily a router that delegates actual step-by-step procedures to references/*.md files (e.g., diagnosis-playbook.md, rag-review-playbook.md), which are outside the scope of this body-only check. The body's own 'Pick the area first' table is a decision/lookup table, not an ordered dependent task list.
tests.evidence: "Name the area, then read its review file before the first API call. Each file holds the router, the step-by-step procedure, the pre-presentation checks..."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The Guardrails section instructs the agent to validate its own output before presenting, e.g. ensuring every finding has a check-id and citation, and bounding/disclosing what was skipped.
tests.evidence: "Evidence or silence. Every finding cites the concrete value that triggered it... A check-id on every finding... Bound the work and disclose what you skipped."
